spec: RFC 9382 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9382.txt) section 6 and Appendix B; docs/plans/client-core/architecture.md 4.7 (bridgit-approver-enrol-v1); spending authority G10.3 X1, X3; written by tools/client-core/spake2-vectors.mjs
note: constants and rfc9382 are the RFC's own values, read from its text by the script and never typed; hex, without the RFC's 0x and line breaks. Every platform recomputes each of them from w, x and y as side A and as side B. bad_shares are shares the named side must refuse (side is the receiver; it holds w and scalar): only the 65-byte uncompressed form of a point on the curve is a share, and a share that makes K the identity is refused. In enrolment the code's maker is side A and the claimer side B, the identities are the two install ids as UTF-8, there is no AAD, and w comes from the enrolment secret (password). enrol.runs: each side present is one device. It holds es, target_name, scalar and its own view of the transcript, receives the values in receives, and must reach expect: accepted, or the first failing check in enrol.reasons order. sends is what that device really sends: its share, RFC confirmation, enrolment confirmation and signatures, made from its own view by the keys in signs (ECDSA P-256 SHA-256, IEEE P1363 r||s, base64). Every received value is one some device in the file sent. In a view, install and approver keys name entries of keys and go into the transcript as SPKI; message and sealing keys go in as the 65-byte point. All keys, secrets, scalars and random values are synthetic.

constants.source: RFC 9382 section 6, the values for P-256, compressed (SEC1)

bad_shares.name: off_curve
bad_shares.why: A valid share with the last bit of y changed

bad_shares.name: identity_encoding
bad_shares.why: The one-byte encoding of the point at infinity

bad_shares.name: compressed
bad_shares.why: A valid point in compressed form: only the 65-byte form is a share

bad_shares.name: hybrid
bad_shares.why: A valid point in the hybrid form (06 or 07)

bad_shares.name: too_short
bad_shares.why: A valid share with its last byte missing

bad_shares.name: too_long
bad_shares.why: A valid share with one byte added

bad_shares.name: x_not_below_p
bad_shares.why: A point on the curve with p added to its x coordinate

bad_shares.name: identity_k
bad_shares.why: The share w*N, sent to A: taking w*N off it leaves the identity, so K is the identity

bad_shares.name: identity_k_for_b
bad_shares.why: The share w*M, sent to B

secret.note: The es field of an approver link: 16 bytes from a secure random source, base64url without padding, 22 characters. Only the spelling an encoder writes is a secret: the last character is one of A, Q, g, w. out_hex null means refused. Nothing is trimmed.

password.note: w is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 of the secret's raw bytes (not its text), salt = label, a newline, the target's registered name (UTF-8), the iteration count of limits.json enrol_pbkdf2_iterations, 40 bytes out, read as a big-endian number and reduced mod the group order n. w is 32 bytes, big-endian.

encoding.note: Transcript: the fields in this order, each behind a 4-byte big-endian length; text is UTF-8, generation is an 8-byte big-endian integer, the random values are 32 bytes, an absent attestation is zero bytes long. The transcript hash is its SHA-256. kex_hash is SHA-256 of "bridgit-approver-enrol-v1 kex", the maker's install id, the claimer's, pA and pB, each behind a 4-byte big-endian length; it is never Hash(TT), which is the key. The enrolment confirmation is HMAC-SHA256 of the transcript hash under the sender's half of HKDF-SHA256(Ke, no salt, info "bridgit-approver-enrol-v1 confirm", 64 bytes): the maker's 32 bytes, then the claimer's. An install key signs "bridgit-approver-enrol-v1 proof", its side (maker or claimer) and the transcript hash, each behind a 4-byte big-endian length. The approver key signs bridgit-owner-auth-v1 bytes: purpose approver_enrol, decision approve, target the other device's install id, approver its own install id, digest the transcript hash, nonce the link id, the transcript's generation, expiry 0.

runs.name: ok_claimer_approver
runs.proves: The claimer becomes the approver; both sides hold the same transcript and every proof checks

runs.name: ok_maker_approver
runs.proves: The maker becomes the approver, with an attestation and a later authority generation

runs.name: wrong_secret
runs.proves: The claimer holds another enrolment secret: the RFC confirmation fails on both sides, and that costs one of the code's five tries

runs.name: wrong_target_name
runs.proves: The claimer was given another registered name for the target: w differs, so the RFC confirmation fails

runs.name: relay_swaps_claimer_install_key
runs.proves: The maker was handed another install key for the claimer, under the claimer's id: the id is not that key's, and the claimer's proofs are over a transcript the maker does not hold

runs.name: relay_swaps_maker_install_key
runs.proves: The claimer was handed another install key for the maker, under the maker's id

runs.name: relay_swaps_install_key_and_id
runs.proves: The maker was handed another install key and its matching id for the claimer: the SPAKE2 identities differ, so the keys do

runs.name: relay_swaps_approver_key
runs.proves: The maker was handed another approver key: the transcripts differ and nothing is stored

runs.name: relay_swaps_sealing_key
runs.proves: The maker was handed another sealing key for the approver

runs.name: relay_swaps_message_key
runs.proves: The claimer was handed another message key for the maker

runs.name: sides_disagree_on_approver
runs.proves: Each side believes it is the approver and names its own approver key

runs.name: generations_disagree
runs.proves: The claimer was told an older authority generation

runs.name: replayed_run
runs.proves: Everything the maker sent in ok_claimer_approver, replayed to a claimer in a new run with the same secret: the claimer's share is fresh, so the old RFC confirmation is for another key

runs.name: replayed_proofs
runs.proves: The same key exchange as ok_claimer_approver, but the claimer's random value is fresh: the maker's earlier proofs are for the earlier transcript

runs.name: install_key_not_held
runs.proves: The claimer names its install key but signs with another: the maker refuses; the claimer cannot tell

runs.name: approver_key_not_held
runs.proves: The claimer names an approver key but signs with another

runs.name: approver_signature_missing
runs.proves: The approver sends no approver-key signature: the owner's check did not happen

runs.name: approver_signature_for_another_purpose
runs.proves: The approver key signed the same fields for approver_add: not an enrolment

self.note: A device enrolling itself as its own approver (spending authority G10.3 X5): the same sixteen fields, encoded the same way, for one install. link_id and kex_hash are zero bytes long; the install id, the install key, the message key and the one 32-byte random value each stand in both the maker's and the claimer's place; approver is "self". There is no key exchange and no confirmation. The install key signs the install proof bytes with side "self". The new approver key signs owner-authorization bytes for approver_enrol: target and approver are both the install id, the digest is the transcript hash, the nonce is the random value in lowercase hex and the expiry is 0. A device stores itself as approver only when its own check of both signatures ends accepted; the reasons are a subset of enrol.reasons, in the same order.

cases.name: ok
cases.proves: The device signs its own transcript with its install key and, after the owner's check, with the new approver key

cases.name: ok_attested_later_generation
cases.proves: With an attestation and a later authority generation (an enrolment after a recovery)

cases.name: install_id_of_another_key
cases.proves: The install id is not the install key's

cases.name: install_key_not_held
cases.proves: The transcript names the install key but another key signed

cases.name: install_proof_of_the_two_device_form
cases.proves: The install key signed as side maker: a proof made for a two-device enrolment is not a self-enrolment

cases.name: approver_key_not_held
cases.proves: The transcript names an approver key but another key signed

cases.name: approver_signature_missing
cases.proves: No approver-key signature: the owner's check did not happen

cases.name: approver_signature_for_another_purpose
cases.proves: The approver key signed the same fields for approver_add: not an enrolment
